chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Baghdadi al-Hafiz narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Karim Abu Abdullah narrated to me, saying: 'Attab (that is, ibn Suhayb) narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Abd Allah al-Umari narrated to me, saying: My father, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them all)'

He said: The Earth was created for seven people; by them they are provided with sustenance, by them rain is sent down, and by them they are granted victory: Abu Dharr, Salman, al-Miqdad, 'Ammar, Hudhayfa, and Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. Ali (peace be upon him) said: And I am their leader, and they are the ones who witnessed the funeral prayer over Fatima (peace be upon her).

The compiler of this book, may God be pleased with him, said: The meaning of his statement 'The Earth was created for seven persons' is not meant from its beginning to its end. Rather, what is meant is that the benefit in the Earth was destined at that time for those who witnessed the funeral prayer over Fatima (peace be upon her). And this is creation by decree (khalq taqdir), not creation by formation (khalq takwin).
ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people for whom the Earth was created according to Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies that this narration refers to 'creative decree' (khalq al-taqdir) rather than physical formation, anchoring the earth's ultimate benefit to the era of Fatima al-Zahra’s funeral prayer. This highlights the theological significance of these seven companions as the primary recipients of divine sustenance and victory, linking their spiritual status directly to the Ahl al-Bayt.
